question: Fractional IPV (fIPV) must NOT be frozen, whereas OPV must be stored frozen; freezing fIPV denatures the antigen and renders it ineffective, making it the most common cold-chain error at the last mile.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The OPV/fIPV distinction is one of the highest-stakes cold-chain facts: OPV = must freeze; fIPV = must NOT freeze. VVM monitors cumulative heat but cannot detect freeze damage — the shake test is used for freeze-sensitive vaccines.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. OPV requires frozen storage (deep freezer, −15°C to −25°C). fIPV is freeze-sensitive and must be stored at +2°C to +8°C (ILR only). Accidental freezing of fIPV is the most common cold-chain error at the outreach session level.
